thread.title: Cigna Deal Lifts S&P 500, Nasdaq Futures; 2 Big Chip Stocks Climb

author: EdJenner
title: Cigna Deal Lifts S&P 500, Nasdaq Futures; 2 Big Chip Stocks Climb
text:
Go to Article 
Dow futures trailed early gains made by the Nasdaq 100 and S&P 500 ahead of Thursday’s start of trade, as chip stocks made some positive moves, Express Scripts ( ESRX ) surged on a merger deal, and earnings reports drove Burlington Stores ( BURL ) and Thor Industries ( THO ) to strong premarket gains. X 
Nasdaq 100 futures rose 0.5%, and S&P 500 futures were up 0.2%, both bolstered by Express Scripts’ huge early leap. Futures for the Dow Jones industrial average battled out of early losses to trade a fraction above fair value, with Intel ( INTC ) and Cisco Systems ( CSCO ) leading. 
Thursday promises no shortage of drama, as legislators continuing wrestling with the White House over tariffs set to be signed into action late today, and as airlines canceled a reported 2,700 flights across the Northeast in response to a snowstorm pummeling the region. 
In overseas markets, stocks surged in Hong Kong, after official data showed China’s export growth accelerated in February to its highest level in three years. The gains sent the Hang Seng index up 1.5%, as the benchmark attempts to stem a two-week decline.

In Japan, Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 posted a more modest 0.5% gain. Trade was mixed in Europe, with the CAC-40 in Paris up 0.4% and Frankfurt’s DAX off 0.3% at midday. 
In the U.S., Thursday’s economic news releases should be limited, with weekly unemployment data the main item on the list. 
The monthly Job Cuts Report from Challenger, Gray & Christmas showed U.S. employers announced 35,369 layoffs in February. That was down 20% from January’s levels, and 4% below the number of layoffs announced a year ago. 
The number of layoffs has now remained below 50,000 for 22 consecutive months, the longest in the gauge’s history. “”The economy is almost at full employment, and companies are holding on to their workforces,” the report noted. Cigna, Express Scripts Deal; Thor, Burlington Up On Earnings 
Chip stocks were in early motion, with Intel up 0.8% to lead the Dow, and as Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) posted a 2% premarket gain. 
Intel ended Wednesday at a new high, atop four straight up days and extended 8% from a 47.40 buy point in a flat base. AMD is testing resistance at its 200-day moving average, ending just below that level after paring its early 9% gain on Wednesday. 
Express Scripts burst 19% higher after Cigna ( CI ) confirmed it would pay $67 billion to acquire the pharmacy benefits manager. Cigna said it expects the deal, which includes $15 billion in debt, to close by the end of the year. 
The move continues a massive round of consolidation and reorganization in the sector, which included CVS Health’s ( CVS ) $68 billion purchase of Aetna ( AET ), the launch of Apple ( AAPL ) health clinics for its employees and a joint venture between Amazon.com ( AMZN ), Berkshire Hathaway ( BRKA ) and JPMorgan ( JPM ) to more efficiently provide healthcare services to their 1 million employees. A year ago, the courts blocked a proposed $48 billion merger between Cigna and health insurer Anthem ( ANTM ). 
Cigna shares dipped 6% in premarket trade. 
In earnings news, Burlington Stores buttoned up an early 9% gain. The New Jersey-based retailer reported late Wednesday fourth-quarter sales, earnings and same-store-sales above consensus projections. Burlington Stores also raised its full-year earnings guidance above analyst targets . The stock is below its 10-week moving average and in the sixth week of a consolidation. 
Thor Industries fiscal second-quarter sales beat analysts’ estimates, while earnings apparently came up short of views. The company said the industry was benefiting from healthy lending standards and credit availability, and from a low rate of charge-offs. Thor shares ended Wednesday 24% below their January high, consolidating just below their 40-week moving average. 
Among IBD 50 stocks , PagSeguro Digital ( PAGS ) rose more than 1%. The Brazil-based payment solutions provider, also an IBD Leaderboard name, is extended from a 30.02 buy point in an IPO base.
